sources.title: Palmyra X5 release announcement, April 28, 2025
sources.evidence: Explicitly announces Palmyra X5 released that day through Writer and Amazon Bedrock. Names Writer as developer and Palmyra as the family, with one-million-token context, image inputs and tool calling.

sources.title: Introducing Palmyra X5
sources.evidence: Exact-model architecture section describes linear and softmax hybrid attention and mixture-of-experts routing. Availability section names Writer API and SDKs; release is April 28, 2025.

sources.title: Writer December 2025 transparency disclosure, items 21, 35 and 41
sources.evidence: Direct HTML disclosure reports 456B total, hybrid Transformer/MoE, and 50B active in final-training FLOP accounting. Item 41 explicitly identifies X5 as closed. Detailed architecture is not disclosed. Indicator examples and evaluator commentary were kept separate from company disclosures.

sources.title: Writer model transparency and regulation statement
sources.evidence: August 27, 2026 statement explicitly identifies X5 as the model covered by Writer’s 2025 FMTI participation, separately from the newer X6 technical report. Confirms provenance and exact-model scope of the submitted disclosure. Full indexed primary text was accessible; direct local fetch returned an unusable page.

sources.title: Current Palmyra model comparison and X5 details
sources.evidence: Exact X5 column specifies 1M context, 8,192 output and adaptive reasoning. X5 details and linked image guide confirm tool use and vision. The current page schedules X4 and X5 deprecation for December 14, 2026.

sources.title: Add images to chat completions
sources.evidence: Native documentation explicitly supports text plus image_url messages with palmyra-x5 and returns text. Examples use the exact model identifier; image support is not inherited from Palmyra Vision or X6.

sources.title: Introducing Action Agent
sources.evidence: The planning-framework section explicitly says Palmyra X5 is used with a new deep-thinking mode enabled. This supports a documented model reasoning mode, while its exposure in each API route remains distinct. Full indexed primary text was accessible; direct local fetch returned an unusable page.

sources.title: Platform services agreement, sections 1(k), 2.1 and 2.3
sources.evidence: Agreement expressly includes model weights and parameters in Writer IP, grants limited non-transferable platform use and reserves ownership. Supports descriptive proprietary classification for the hosted model.

sources.title: Bedrock Palmyra X5 API limits
sources.evidence: Serving documentation lists exact writer.palmyra-x5-v1:0, April 28 release, text modality, 1,040,000 input tokens and 8,192 output. These route-specific limits differ from the native Writer model contract and do not erase native image support.

sources.title: Palmyra x6 Technical Report, version 3
sources.evidence: Read the complete later technical report and its architecture table. It contains no X5-labeled parameter comparison; its 744B/40B GLM-5.2-derived X6 specifications are not transferred to X5.

sources.title: Native chat completion API
sources.evidence: Exact X5 request examples and schemas support tools and text/image content. The published request schema has no separate thinking toggle; response accounting includes reasoning_tokens. This does not establish identical reasoning controls across every provider.

sources.title: FMTI 2025 disclosure methodology
sources.evidence: Methodology distinguishes developer-submitted transparency reports from six manually gathered company reports. Writer is among the participating submitters, consistent with its own explicit participation statement.

name.note: Exact model name and palmyra-x5 API identity.

developer.note: Developer’s launch and ownership statement identify Writer.

family.note: Explicitly a member of the Palmyra model family.

release_date.note: Dated developer announcement explicitly says available that day on Writer and Bedrock. Searches for earlier exact-model previews did not establish an earlier release; later provider listing dates are not used.

open_weights.note: The exact-model disclosure expressly calls X5 closed; contracted access is not public weight distribution.

license.note: Descriptive classification under restricted commercial access and retained model intellectual property.

parameters_b.note: Author-reported total from the X5 transparency submission. Nominal disclosure, not an independently counted checkpoint.

active_parameters_b.note: Explicit N_active value used for final-training compute estimation. Serving activity is not separately specified; proposed phase scope preserves this limitation.

architecture.note: Developer explicitly describes a decoder-only hybrid-attention Transformer with expert routing. Layer counts and expert configuration are undisclosed.

context_window.note: Preserve native Writer’s explicit one-million-token context. Bedrock documents 1,040,000 input tokens for its route; do not silently conflate these contracts.

modalities.note: Exact native X5 guide supports text/image inputs and text output. Structured output is text, and the Bedrock text-only route is not a model-wide restriction.

reasoning.note: Developer explicitly describes X5 deep-thinking mode in Action Agent, beyond generic benchmark reasoning ability. Native public request schema does not expose a separate thinking toggle; no claim of uniform provider controls or tested endpoint behavior.

tool_call.note: Developer announcement and exact API schema document tool/function calling.

description.value: Writer mixture-of-experts model with hybrid attention, text and image input, a one-million-token context window and tool calling.
description.note: Replaces vague reasoning-focused prose with documented architecture and native API properties.

Writer model transparency and regulation statement
Current Palmyra model comparison and X5 details

patch.notes: Writer reports 456B total parameters. Its X5 transparency submission uses 50B active parameters in final-training compute accounting; no separate serving-phase active count is given. Counts are author disclosures, not checkpoint measurements. Native Writer documents a one-million-token context and image input; Bedrock lists 1,040,000 input tokens and text-only access. Deep-thinking mode is documented in Action Agent, while API controls vary. Released April 28, 2025; current native documentation schedules deprecation for December 14, 2026.

summary: Added nominal 456B total and phase-qualified 50B active from Writer’s X5 transparency submission, MoE architecture and proprietary classification. Confirmed launch and native capabilities; retained route differences and scheduled deprecation. Later X6 specifications are not transferred.
